Are you frustrated for 2026 H1B application because you don't have an advanced degree?

Don't worry, your immigration lawyer may tell you that you may need an H1B Expert Opinion Letter to show USCIS that you have the US equivalence of an advanced degree.

But what's an Expert Opinion Letter (EOL)?

This article is to break everything down for you if you have any questions about the H1B Expert Opinion Letter.

Founded by an immigrant just like you, AET knows your struggles. So read on the 8 key things to know for your H1B Expert Opinion Letter.

1. What is an H1B Expert Opinion Letter?

Expert Opinion Letter (EOL), aka Professional Experience Evaluation, is written by university professors or experts to pair your relevant professional experience with academic coursework to determine a U.S. degree equivalency.

It's widely used for Eb1a, Eb2-NIW, H1B (or H1B RFE), TN-Visa and other immigration related cases.

You may have to request this service if you didn't finsh a four-year higher education program in your home country but have many years of work experience in your field.

USCIS needs this as proof that you have a US equivalent advanced degree.

2. Why do you need H1B Expert Opinion Letter?

According to USCIS, you are required to have at least an advanced degree or its equivalent for an H1B visa.

There are two main reasons why you may need an H1B Expert Opinion Letter:

H1B Application

As we mentioned in the beginning, if you don't have an advanced degree but are applying for an H1B, then you may need work experience to support your applicaiton.

Typically, evaluators will use the 3-in-1 rule to determine your U.S. equivalency.

H1B Request for Evidence (RFE)

According to PROVAL, there're top 5 reasons for an H1B RFE:
1. Specialty occupation position
2. Employer-employee relationship
3. Availability of work off-site
4. Beneficiary qualifications
5. Maintenance of status

Therefore, you may need an H1B Expert Opinion Letter to showcase the evidence that you either have a U.S advanced degree or that your foreign degree plus years of work experience is equivalent to a particular U.S degree.

5. Documents for H1B Expert Opinion Letters

Before you start the process of evaluating your credentials, you may need the following documents for the H1B Expert Opinion Letter:

  • Degree Certificate or Diploma
  • Translated degree certificate by a certified translator
  • Resume and Employment Verification Letters if possible
  • Transcript and its certied English translation (can be supporting documents)

6. What does an H1B Expert Opinion Letter include?

An Expert Opinion Letter for H1B usually includes:

  • Introduction: Explanation of the purpose of the letter; A statement identifying the expert, their qualifications, and their relationship to the petitioner.
  • Expert’s Qualifications: Detailed description of the expert’s background, including academic credentials, professional experience, and any relevant accomplishments or recognition.
  • Petitioner’s (Your) Background: Description of the petitioner’s specific work, projects, research contribution, and more.
  • National Interest Criteria: Explanation of why the petitioner’s work is of substantial intrinsic merit.
  • Examples: Specific examples of the impact and importance of the petitioner’s work.
  • Conclusion: A summary reiterating the key points made in the letter; A clear statement supporting the approval of the NIW petition.
